Introducing Kachava's new 3-in-1 digestive boost. Simply mix into your favorite Kachava shake or any cold beverage.
Go to Kachava.com and use code NPR for 15% off your first order. That's K-A-C-H-A-V-A.com. Code NPR.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Cora Vekulman. Russian and Ukrainian officials are holding U.S.-sponsored peace talks in Abu Dhabi.
It's the first such meeting since February, and it comes as the White House pushes for a broader peace deal.
From Moscow, NPR's Charles Mains has details.
Publicly, Russia has shown no flexibility in its demands for Ukraine to surrender large swathes of its territory. Yet the Abu Dhabi talks come shortly after President Trump hosted a senior Kremlin envoy at the White House, after which Trump suggested a wider peace deal was within reach.
U.S. officials speaking on background tell NPR part of the discussions will focus on creating a new long-term security architecture between Russia and Europe, believing that could unlock concessions from both Kiev and Moscow.
Such talk has unnerved U.S. allies in Europe who plan to send their own teams to Abu Dhabi, where they'll hold consultations with Ukraine and American officials on the sidelines.
Charles Mains, NPR News, Moscow.
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is scheduled to hold a press conference in about two hours.
He's expected to address the articles of impeachment filed against him yesterday by Republican Congressman Thomas Massey of Kentucky.
NPR's Sam Greenglass says Massey filed eight articles in all.
Four focus on Hegseth circumventing or ignoring Congress's authority over waging war, mostly with regard to the war on Iran, but also Yemen.
One article accuses Hegseth of committing extrajudicial killings when the administration carried out strikes on alleged drug boats in the Caribbean Sea.
Another claims Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro was seized without legal authority. And another focuses on Hegseth retaliating against Senator Mark Kelly, who encouraged members of the military to disobey illegal orders.
NPR's Sam Greenglass reporting Hegseth has called the impeachment articles a sham.
President Trump says he supports Hegseth.
Today is the deadline for any outstanding ballots in Mississippi to be addressed. Said a Democratic challenger, Scott Colom, leads Republican incumbent Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith by about 2,500 votes.
From Mississippi Public Broadcasting, Kristin Kahler reports.
The race still hasn't been called, but about 97 percent of ballots have now been counted.
In Hines County, which includes parts of Metro Jackson, Election Commissioner Cadotta Brown says she wants people to understand accuracy is more important than speed.
The integrity of this matter is more important than anything. So that's why I ask everyone to be patient and give us a little grace.
Mail-in and affidavit ballots, also known as provisional ballots, are still being counted.
The deadline for those to be accepted is Tuesday. Counties have until Friday to certify complete results.
The Mississippi Secretary of State's office has not responded to requests for updated information on the ballot count.
For NPR News, I'm Kristin Kahler in Jackson, Mississippi.
This is NPR.
The chairs of three House committees have sent a letter to NVIDIA's CEO Jensen Huang.
They're asking him to appear behind closed doors to answer questions about his interactions with an alleged Chinese spy.
Huang has admitted to a romantic relationship. NVIDIA has opened its own internal investigation.
New research suggests that reducing air pollution in line with recommendations by the World Health Organization could save nine million lives a year.
And Piers Jonathan Lambert reports, the vast majority of people live under conditions that exceed those guidelines.
Air pollution spewed by power plants, factories or cars is seriously bad for health.
Studies show it can raise risk of ailments as diverse as heart disease and dementia.
In light of that research, the WHO issued tighter guidelines on air pollution in 2021.
A new study in the journal Environment International estimates meeting those guidelines could have big benefits for low and middle income countries.
They found that 9.4 million deaths, mostly due to heart disease and stroke, could be averted each year under the guidelines.
In addition, cutting air pollution could prevent millions of new cases of these diseases from ever developing.
Those potential benefits are far off for many, however, as the WHO estimates that over 90 percent of the global population lives in places that don't meet current guidelines.
Jonathan Lambert, NPR News.
The winner of this year's Booker Prize in fiction is British writer M. John Harrison.
He's been honored for his science fiction novel, The End of Everything.
The novel features themes of apocalypse.
You're listening to NPR.
